hard.q: Gisteren hebben we ___ op het feest in Antwerpen echt goed geamuseerd.
hard.e: Con we il riflessivo è ons, anche al passato prossimo e con l'inversione. onszelf non si usa con un verbo veramente riflessivo come zich amuseren.

g.zich: si: solo per lui, lei, loro e u
g.onszelf: noi stessi: non con un verbo riflessivo vero

hard.tt: Ieri alla festa ad Anversa ci siamo divertiti davvero tanto.

hard.q: Sorry, ik ___ me vergist: de tram naar het station vertrekt pas om kwart over acht.
hard.e: Trabocchetto italiano: "mi sono sbagliato", ma in olandese i riflessivi vogliono sempre hebben: ik heb me vergist.

g.ben: sono: i riflessivi non vogliono zijn
g.is: è: soggetto sbagliato e ausiliare sbagliato
g.word: divento: non è un ausiliare del passato prossimo

hard.tt: Scusa, mi sono sbagliato: il tram per la stazione parte solo alle otto e un quarto.

hard.q: Vanmorgen heeft Pieter ___ niet geschoren, want hij was te laat.
a: zich
hard.e: hij → zich. Con l'inversione il riflessivo viene subito dopo il soggetto: heeft Pieter zich niet geschoren.
hard.tt: Stamattina Pieter non si è rasato, perché era in ritardo.

hard.q: Waarom ___ jullie je zo? De trein naar Brugge vertrekt pas om tien uur.
a: haasten
hard.e: jullie vuole il verbo al plurale (haasten) e il riflessivo je, non zich.
hard.tt: Perché vi affrettate così? Il treno per Bruges parte solo alle dieci.

hard.q: Stamattina mi sono vestito in fretta.
hard.a: Vanmorgen heb ik me snel aangekleed
alt: Ik heb me vanmorgen snel aangekleed
hard.e: hebben (non zijn) + riflessivo dopo il soggetto; aankleden è separabile: participio aangekleed, in fondo.
hard.tt: Stamattina mi sono vestito in fretta.

hard.q: Mio fratello non si ricorda più il nome della sua insegnante.
hard.a: Mijn broer herinnert zich de naam van zijn lerares niet meer
alt: Mijn broer herinnert zich niet meer de naam van zijn lerares
hard.e: zich herinneren: zich subito dopo il verbo; con un oggetto determinato (de naam) niet meer va di solito dopo l'oggetto.
hard.tt: Mio fratello non si ricorda più il nome della sua insegnante.

en.note:
The idea

Dutch has reflexive verbs, where the subject does the action to itself, like English "wash yourself" or "enjoy yourself". They're built with a reflexive pronoun, the equivalent of myself, yourself, himself... The big difference from English: many verbs that are not reflexive in English are reflexive in Dutch, and the short pronoun is used all the time (ik was me = I wash, I get washed). The pronoun goes after the verb, just like an English object.

The reflexive pronouns

subjectreflexiveexample
ikme (mij)ik was me
jijjejij wast je
uzich / uu wast zich
hij / zij / hetzichhij wast zich
wijonswij wassen ons
julliejejullie wassen je
zij (they)zichzij wassen zich

As you can see, they're almost the same as the object pronouns (unit 4). The only new form is zich, for he, she, they and formal u: it covers himself, herself, itself, themselves. With u you can say both u vergist zich and u vergist u. With jullie the reflexive is je. mij instead of me is used for emphasis or in a more formal style (in Belgium it's common in speech too).

Where the pronoun goes

  • Right after the conjugated verb: Ik voel me goed. (I feel good)
  • With inversion it comes after the subject: Vandaag voel ik me goed.
  • In questions with je you get "je" twice: Voel je je goed? The first is the subject (you), the second the reflexive (yourself).
  • With a modal the infinitive goes to the end: Ik moet me haasten. (I have to hurry)
  • With a separable verb the particle goes to the end: Ik kleed me aan. (I get dressed)

The perfect takes hebben

Reflexive verbs always form the perfect with hebben, as in English: Ik heb me vergist (I was wrong, I made a mistake), We hebben ons geamuseerd (we had a good time).

Reflexive in Dutch, not in English

This is the real challenge for English speakers: many everyday verbs need a reflexive pronoun in Dutch where English has none. Hurry = zich haasten (ik haast me), remember = zich herinneren, be wrong = zich vergissen, be bored = zich vervelen, get dressed = zich aankleden, shave = zich scheren, worry = zich zorgen maken. That's why it's best to learn these verbs together with zich, as in the word list. On the other hand, "be called" is simply heten (ik heet Luca), and get up = opstaan, sit down = gaan zitten.

Zichzelf: himself, herself

Adding -zelf gives the emphatic form, like English "myself, himself": mezelf, jezelf, zichzelf, onszelf. It's used with verbs that aren't normally reflexive, especially after a preposition: Hij denkt alleen aan zichzelf (he only thinks of himself). With truly reflexive verbs it isn't used: ik vergis mezelf → ik vergis me.

Watch out: typical mistakes for English speakers

  • Leaving out the reflexive: Ik haast → Ik haast me (I'm hurrying); Ik voel goed → Ik voel me goed.
  • Using the -zelf form everywhere, like English "myself": Ik vergis mezelf → Ik vergis me.
  • Using zich with everyone: Wij wassen zich → Wij wassen ons.
  • Making "be called" reflexive: Ik heet me Luca → Ik heet Luca.
en.vlaams: With gij/ge the reflexive is u: "Ge moet u niet haasten" (you don't have to hurry). Before a party in Flanders you'll often hear "Amuseer u!" or "Amuseer je!", meaning "have fun!".

items.e: ik → me: ik voel me. Unlike English "I don't feel well", Dutch needs the reflexive.

drills.q: Which verb is reflexive in Dutch?
drills.e: zich vergissen = to be mistaken. Heten (to be called), opstaan (to get up) and vergeten (to forget) are not reflexive in Dutch.

g.vergissen: to be mistaken: zich vergissen, reflexive

g.zich: himself/herself: only for he, she, they

0.t: Are you sick? — Yes, I don't feel well.

2.t: We're hurrying, because the train is leaving.

g.vergis: I'm mistaken: with u you need the -t

g.Mij heet Luca: the subject is ik, not mij

hard.q: Gisteren hebben we ___ op het feest in Antwerpen echt goed geamuseerd.
hard.e: With we the reflexive is ons, also in the perfect and after inversion. onszelf (ourselves) isn't used with a truly reflexive verb like zich amuseren.

g.zich: himself/herself/themselves: only for hij, zij and u
g.onszelf: ourselves (emphatic): not with a true reflexive verb

hard.tt: Yesterday we really had a great time at the party in Antwerp.

hard.q: Sorry, ik ___ me vergist: de tram naar het station vertrekt pas om kwart over acht.
hard.e: Reflexive verbs always take hebben in the perfect, just like English "I have made a mistake": ik heb me vergist.

g.is: is: wrong subject and wrong auxiliary

hard.tt: Sorry, I was wrong: the tram to the station doesn't leave until a quarter past eight.

hard.q: Vanmorgen heeft Pieter ___ niet geschoren, want hij was te laat.
a: zich
hard.e: hij → zich. Unlike English "he didn't shave", Dutch needs the reflexive. After inversion it comes right after the subject: heeft Pieter zich niet geschoren.
hard.tt: Pieter didn't shave this morning, because he was late.

hard.q: Waarom ___ jullie je zo? De trein naar Brugge vertrekt pas om tien uur.
a: haasten
hard.e: jullie takes the plural verb (haasten) and the reflexive je, not zich.
hard.tt: Why are you (all) in such a hurry? The train to Bruges doesn't leave until ten.

hard.q: This morning I got dressed quickly.
hard.a: Vanmorgen heb ik me snel aangekleed
alt: Ik heb me vanmorgen snel aangekleed
hard.e: "Get dressed" = zich aankleden, with hebben; the reflexive comes after the subject. aankleden is separable: participle aangekleed, at the end.
hard.tt: This morning I got dressed quickly.

hard.q: My brother no longer remembers his teacher's name.
hard.a: Mijn broer herinnert zich de naam van zijn lerares niet meer
alt: Mijn broer herinnert zich niet meer de naam van zijn lerares
hard.e: "Remember" is reflexive in Dutch: zich herinneren, with zich right after the verb. With a definite object (de naam), niet meer usually goes after the object.
hard.tt: My brother no longer remembers his teacher's name.
